findings.title: ESC1 - Misconfigured Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template allows enrollee to specify Subject Alternative Name (SAN) and has client authentication EKU, enabling privilege escalation to any user/computer.

findings.title: ESC4 - Certificate Template ACL Review Required
findings.description: Certificate templates with authentication capability should be reviewed for overly permissive ACLs that allow non-admins to modify template properties.

details.note: Full ACL analysis requires parsing nTSecurityDescriptor. Manual review recommended.

findings.title: ESC9 - No Security Extension in Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate templates using schema version 1 do not include the szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT security extension. Combined with weak certificate mapping, this allows certificate impersonation attacks.

details.recommendation: Upgrade certificate templates to schema version 2 or higher, and enable strong certificate mapping.

findings.title: ESC3 - Enrollment Agent Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template allows issuance of enrollment agent certificates, which can be used to enroll certificates on behalf of other users.

findings.title: ESC2 - Any Purpose Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template has "Any Purpose" EKU or no EKU constraints, allowing issued certificates to be used for any purpose including client authentication.

findings.title: ESC6 - CA Configuration Review Required
findings.description: Certificate Authorities should be checked for EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 flag which allows any certificate requestor to specify a SAN.

details.note: Check registry key EditFlags on CA servers. Flag 0x00040000 indicates vulnerability.

findings.title: ESC7 - CA ACL Review Required
findings.description: Certificate Authority ACLs should be reviewed for ManageCA or ManageCertificates rights granted to non-administrators.

details.note: Manual review of CA ACLs recommended.

findings.title: ESC10 - Certificate Mapping Configuration Review Required
findings.description: Domain controllers should be configured for strong certificate mapping to prevent certificate impersonation attacks. This setting cannot be detected via LDAP.

details.note: Check StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement registry key on DCs. Value should be 2 (Full Enforcement).
details.recommendation: Set StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement to 2 for full enforcement. Test in compatibility mode (1) first.

findings.title: ESC11 - RPC Encryption Enforcement Check Required
findings.description: Certificate Authorities should enforce RPC encryption (IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST flag) to prevent NTLM relay attacks to the ICertPassage RPC interface.

details.note: Check InterfaceFlags registry key on CA servers. Flag 0x00000200 (IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST) should be set.
details.recommendation: Set IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST flag using: certutil -setreg CA\InterfaceFlags +IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST

findings.title: ESC5 - PKI Object ACL Review Required
findings.description: PKI-related AD objects should be reviewed for overly permissive ACLs that could allow non-admins to modify CA configuration or templates.

details.note: Manual review of PKI object ACLs recommended.

findings.title: ESC8 - Web Enrollment Check Required
findings.description: Certificate Authorities should be checked for HTTP-based web enrollment endpoints which are vulnerable to NTLM relay attacks.

details.note: Check for http://<CA>/certsrv/ endpoints. HTTPS with Extended Protection mitigates this.

findings.title: GPO Permissions Review Required
findings.description: Group Policy Objects should be reviewed for overly permissive ACLs that allow non-administrators to modify GPO settings.

details.note: Manual review of GPO ACLs recommended. Check for non-admin principals with write access.

findings.title: Potentially Orphaned GPOs
findings.description: GPOs that may be orphaned (missing SYSVOL content or AD object). Orphaned GPOs can cause processing errors and may indicate tampering.

details.recommendation: Compare AD GPOs with SYSVOL folders. Use gpotool.exe or Get-GPO to identify orphans. Delete orphaned GPOs after verification.

findings.title: GPO Applies to All Authenticated Users
findings.description: GPOs with Authenticated Users granted the "Apply Group Policy" permission. This is the default but may be too broad for sensitive policies.

details.recommendation: Review if all GPOs should apply to all users. Consider using security filtering for sensitive policies.
details.note: This is informational - Authenticated Users is the default.

findings.title: LAPS Not Deployed via GPO
findings.description: No active Group Policy Object was found deploying LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution). This leaves local admin passwords vulnerable to reuse attacks.

details.recommendation: Deploy LAPS via GPO to manage local administrator passwords.

findings.title: Weak Password Policy
findings.description: Domain password policy requires only 7 characters minimum. Microsoft recommends at least 12 characters for standard accounts, 14+ for privileged accounts.

findings.title: Unlinked Group Policy Objects
findings.description: GPOs exist that are not linked to any OU, domain, or site. These may be orphaned or indicate incomplete deployment.
